## Checklist

The pull request touches the public API:

- [ ] The change was discussed in an "API proposal" issue: #
- [ ] Tests are in `commonTest` and pass in CI.
- [ ] The ABI dump is updated (`./gradlew updateKotlinAbi`) and the change in it was looked at in review.
- [ ] An entry in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- [ ] A hot path is touched: a benchmark before and after (`./gradlew :benchmarks:quickBenchmark` with a suite filter); a slowdown of more than 10 % is explained.
- [ ] A new dependency is agreed with the maintainers.

Any pull request:

- [ ] `./gradlew check` passes (at least with `-Pcalendrum.targets=jvm`; with `all` if the pull request touches the build, the targets or other platforms).
- [ ] A dependency, plugin or build tool is added or raised: `verification-metadata.xml` is updated with the command from CONTRIBUTING.md,
  and the group, name, version and `origin` of the new entries are checked (entries added by Gradle say "Generated by Gradle").
- [ ] The description says what the pull request added or changed in the build, the tests, the benchmarks and CI.
- [ ] The implementation differs from what was agreed in the issue or the API proposal, and the difference is described here.

## CI

The repository is private and CI minutes are limited.

- Until the maintainers turn on automatic runs, workflows are started only by hand. Before merging, start the Linux set by hand
  or run the same tasks locally (`./gradlew check`).
- Once they are on, every pull request gets only the Linux jobs. Labels turn on the expensive sets: `ci:native` (Kotlin/Native on
  Linux: the `linuxX64` tests, compiling the Apple klibs), `ci:macos` (the Apple tests), `ci:windows` (the `mingwX64` tests).
  Set a label only when the pull request touches those platforms: macOS uses minutes ×10, Windows ×2.
